name: smwsprites-1-up-mushroom
title: 1-Up + Mushroom
description: This is a disassembly of sprites 74 and 78 in SMW - Mushroom and 1-Up.

name: smwsprites-3-up-moon-sprite-v2
title: 3-UP Moon Sprite V2.0
description:
3-UP Moon Sprite V2.0:

Description: A sprite that tries to mimic the 3-UP Moon Object tile from SMW, but in sprite form! It's a bit different from the existing one, it acts with new behaviours! obviously, this will works like the Object tile, but you can add/modify stuff!

Features:
PIXI Support/Compatibility.
SA-1 Support/Compatibility.
JSON Support.
A documentation (Readme) file.
Allow customize the sprite easily with an Extra Byte.

More details are on the documentation (Readme) file!

Requested by NopeContest

name: smwsprites-32x32-boo-block
title: 32x32 Boo Block
description: This is a Boo Block that is 32x32 instead of the normal 16x16.  That about sums it up, really.  It's based off my disassembly of the Boo Block.

name: smwsprites-32x32-chain-chomp
title: 32x32 Chain Chomp
description:
This sprite will jump towards you, and after 8 jumps will dash into you and then fall off-screen. Demonstration video: http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4BBVCdxRm24

Credit would be appreciated but isn't necessary.

SA-1 hybrid. Setting the extra bit makes the last dash auto-aim in Mario's direction.

Graphics made by Mathos. Please credit :3

name: smwsprites-32x32-coin
title: 32x32 coin
description:
A coin 32x32 in size in the form of a sprite. It's pretty easy to customise it into another collectable too.
Must provide your own graphics.

name: smwsprites-32x32-goal-point-question-sphere
title: 32x32 Goal Point Question Sphere
description: This is a 32x32 version of the Goal Point Question Sphere (sprite 4A). It also has some customizable features, such as the exit type, being affected by gravity, and even being collected by other sprites. Check out the .asm file for all the customization options. Replaces the Digging Chuck in GFX05.

name: smwsprites-32x32-info-box
title: 32x32 Info Box
description:
This is a large 32x32 version of the Info Box sprite (B9), that will display a message when hit from below. Unlike the vanilla sprite however, this version can display messages from any level ($13BF format) with extra byte 1, and uses the extra bit to determine whether it shows message 1 or 2, instead of it's X position. You can also optionally make the Info Box vanish after being hit, or teleport Mario via the screen exit.
See the .asm file for customization options and usage notes.

Insert the Clipping.asm file into PIXI's "routines" folder before inserting the sprite. Credit goes to imamelia, lx5 and TheBiob for this routine.

name: smwsprites-32x32-throw-block
title: 32x32 Throw Block
description:
This is a 32x32 throw block, it acts just like a regular one except, it will shake the ground when hitting the wall, and it will go in a diagonal when being kicked up. If the extra bit is set the player won't be able to move when holding it.

Tester's note: Could use some fitting special effects (those that the regular throw blocks have too). But other than that a pretty neat sprite.

Now SA-1 hybrid.

name: smwsprites-64x64-moving-castle-block
title: 64x64 Moving Castle Block
description:
A 64x64 variant of the moving castle block platform. Can be set to start going left or right by the extra bit, and the amount of time it can move or stay quiet can also be configured by the extra bytes.
Using NMSTL or MaxTile (included in The SA-1 Pack) is recommended.

Requested by Knight of Time during C3 Winter 2025.

name: smwsprites-abyssal-fish
title: Abyssal Fish
description:
This fish moves casually in a zig-zag manner in a set pattern (big horizontal step with some upward speed, big upward step with some horizontal speed, big horizontal step with some downward speed, big downward step with some horizontal speed).

Check the readme file for customisation options.

name: smwsprites-acro
title: Acro
description:
This is the underwater boss from Kirby. He swims around the level and spawns hooks, skulls, and mini Acros. The player can pick up the skulls and throw them at Acro to hurt him. By default, the boss dies after 3 hits.

Make sure to specify the sprite number of the hook, the mini Acro, and the skull in acro.asm! Check the ASM files for customization options.

name: smwsprites-activate-bowser-scene
title: Activate Bowser Scene
description:
A disassembly of Bowser (sprite A0), commented and ready to be inserted with PIXI.

Please note that the level mode should be set to 10 and the sprite memory to 00 for the sprite to work correctly.

Check the ASM file for customization options, especially if you're using AddmusicK.

name: smwsprites-adventure-island-coyote
title: Adventure Island - Coyote
description:
A coyote from Adventure Island. A flower is spawned in its place, and if player goes far enough past it, Coyote will spawn and try to catch up to the player. The color of the flower dictates what kind of coyote it'll be (Red - regular, Blue - jumps over hazards, Yellow - chases player, Green - very fast).

A standalone version is also included.

Requested by Blizzard Buffalo.

name: smwsprites-adventure-island-egg
title: Adventure Island - Egg
description:
This is an egg that acts like an egg from Adventure Island (or Wonder Boy port for the NES, if you will). When you touch it, it launches upward with x-speed depending on player's. And when it lands back, it spawns a sprite.

Credit is optional.

name: smwsprites-adventure-island-fruit
title: Adventure Island - Fruit
description:
This is a fruit from Adventure Island for the NES. It'll appear after a set amount of time, and disappear shortly after. When picked up, it'll add some time to the timer.

Credit is optional.

name: smwsprites-adventure-island-rock
title: Adventure Island - Rock
description:
This is a rock object from Adventure Island for the NES. When in contact, it'll trip the player, disabling their control untill they land on a solid surface, and deduct some seconds from the timer.

Credit is optional.

name: smwsprites-air-bubble-shooter
title: Air Bubble Shooter
description:
This shooter will shoot the small air bubbles you see in water levels. It has two variations. One of them will spawn the bubbles at a fixed interval, the other will spawn them at a random interval.

Note: The level must be a water level or the bubbles won't spawn. Sprite buoyancy isn't required though.

Requested by Final Theory.

name: smwsprites-alarm-turret
title: Alarm Turret
description:
This consists of three sprites, based on the alarm system in Magna Centipede's stage from Mega Man X2.

The spotlights will travel left/right or up/down (depending on the extra bit) and optionally flash at 60 FPS (which makes them look transparent; the GIF is not smooth enough to show the real effect). When Mario touches one, it will set the On/Off switch to Off and optionally disappear. After about 3 seconds, the switch will be set back to on.

Also included is a turret, which will fall to the ground and shoot projectiles when Mario gets spotted. Make sure to specify the sprite number of the projectile in alarm_turret.asm!

Check the ASM files for customization options.

Usage with No More Sprite Tile Limits is recommended because the spotlights are 64x64 sprites.

Due to the locking system (which lets you put more than one spotlight on screen), the spotlights write values above 1 to $14AF (On/Off switch flag), which may cause issues with improperly coded ASM resources.

name: smwsprites-albatoss-albatoss-bomber
title: Albatoss + Albatoss Bomber
description: Albatoss by mikeyk converted to PIXI, it can drop bombs (or other sprite) or torpedos and drop with some delay depending of what extension bytes are used (Values that you can use: 00, 01, 04, 05, 80, 81, 84 and 85).

name: smwsprites-albatoss-bomber-boss
title: Albatoss Bomber Boss
description:
An Albatoss Bomber who takes 3 hits (by thrown objects) to defeat. Additionally, it can walk faster after each HP. It will change direction after crossing 16 units of blocks (1 screen).

You can increase the HP by setting the value of HP_COUNTER to something else in the INIT routine. Make sure you increase the number of bytes in the "RightSp" table if you do that though.

Requested by SomeGuy

name: smwsprites-alternate-dkc-like-barrels
title: Alternate DKC-like Barrels
description:
Just in time for Christmas, here are more DKC-like barrels. These DKC like barrels are similar to what is found in both DKC Vine Valley and DKC2 Bramble Blast. They have three set directions unlike the 360 degree barrels already submitted and can make for newer puzzles in SMW.

Check the video below
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EL0o90ktZwI

name: smwsprites-amazing-flying-hammer-bro-stationary-smw-hammer-bro
title: Amazing Flying Hammer Bro + Stationary SMW Hammer Bro
description:
This is the Amazing Flying Hammer Bro (sprite x9B) from Super Mario World, disassembled and slightly adjusted for ease-of-use.
This variety does not lock to the winged block platform like the vanilla sprite, as this behavior is tied to the platform itself.
A disassembled and modified version of the Flying Blocks (sprite x9C) is included if you'd like to make use of it, but is not as customizable as TheBiob's disassembly. It is tailored to work alongside this sprite fairly seamlessly, however.

To give a brief explanation as to how the vanilla sprite operates:
- While the sprite is alive, the graphics routine is not loaded.
- The winged block platform, when a "living" Hammer Bro exists, will render a copy of the the Hammer Bro's graphics routine. This prevents a weird 1-frame "desync" between the sprites if the Hammer Bro happens to fall on specific sprite slots.

This version renders the graphics routine at all times. If the platform is being used, you'll simply need to ensure the Hammer Bro is placed or moved after the platform (so that it appears "in front of" the platform in Lunar Magic). This should resolve most desync issues.

Release History:
- 7/6/2009: v1.0 - Initial Release.
- 12/12/2023: v2.0 - New disassembly created.

versions.title: Amazing Flying Hammer Bro + Stationary SMW Hammer Bro

name: smwsprites-amazing-flying-puntin-chuck
title: Amazing Flying Puntin' Chuck
description:
A hybrid of the Amazing Flying Hammer Bro and Chargin' Chuck enemies.
If placed above sprite x9C, it will lock onto the platform -- otherwise it will simply fall onto whatever is placed under it.
If stomped, it will take damage like a Chargin' Chuck -- animation included. Hitting x9C's blocks from below will also damage the enemy (complete with a new animation).
Do note that this sprite, being based on Chargin' Chucks, will die instantly if hit from below by normal blocks.

There are a few base customizations through the use of the "Extension" field when inserting the sprite:
- Extra Byte 1 will define how much HP the Chuck has. If set to xFF it will be invincible to stomps/hits from below. If set to x00 it will default to 3 hits.
- Extra Byte 2 will define how frequently the Chuck throws a sprite.
- Extra Byte 3 will define which sprite the Chuck throws, from a list. The default values for this are as follows:
--- x00 - Next sprite in your list.txt.
--- x01 - Exploding Bob-Omb.
--- x02 - Hammer Bros.' Hammer
--- x03 - Spiny Egg
New entries can be created if desired.

GFX made by wuffalo, albeit slightly modified to fit the graphics routine.

name: smwsprites-angry-star
title: Angry Star
description:
This star, inspired in the Super Mario Land 2, moves following a "infinity" curve. It's indestructible unless hit while Mario has star power. If the extra bit is set, the star will explode after a set amount of cycles.

Check the readme file for customisation options.

name: smwsprites-angry-sun-happy-moon-v1
title: Angry Sun/Happy Moon (v1.3)
description:
The Angry Sun from Super Mario Bros. 3 (and Super Mario Maker 2). It's locked on the screen horizontally and remains dormant until Mario reaches a certain screen (customizable with the first extra property byte), at which point it starts spinning in circles and swooping down in attempt to hurt Mario. It can be killed with a star or a thrown object.

If the Extra Property Byte 2's first bit (i.e. set it to 1) is set, it will instead use the Super Mario Maker 2 graphics set and animations.

Setting the Extra Bit will cause the sprite to look and act like the Happy Moon enemy from Super Mario Maker 2. Touching it will cause it to instantly kill all sprites that are not set to "Invincible to star/cape/fire/bouncing blk". Do note that while the SMB3 graphics are in effect, the Happy Moon will NOT display properly. You will need to remap the sprite if you wish to have the Happy Moon and SMB3 Angry Sun available in the same ExGFX file.

The initial position of the sprite is determined by setting the Y position of the sprite. If it is an even number, it'll appear on the left side. If it's odd, it'll appear on the right.

Note that this sprite disables L/R scrolling for any level it's put into in order to prevent an issue with following the screen.

name: smwsprites-annoying-bee
title: Annoying Bee
description:
Inspired by a type of bee encountered at Wario Land 2, this bee starts moving in a sinusoidal-like pattern. When Mario gets into a customisable vertical and horizontal range, the bee stops moving some frames and then starts following Mario.

The download includes the original WL2 graphics, recolored to fit the Super Mario World style.

This sprite does not work well with upside down slopes, so take that into account when planning setups with it.

Updated with a better screenshot, PIXI version and slightly better code.

name: smwsprites-anti-starman
title: Anti-Starman
description:
This Star works like the original, but it Will damage or kill the player if touch her. There are a bit of settings and defines that can be change in the .asm like:

1.- Tilemap.
2.- Flash Animation.
3.- X/Y Speed to change the arc.

This Sprite is based in the SMW Star dissamble Made by RussianMan, Credit is optional, but it's would be nice.

There are two examples .gif to see how this sprite works and a one screenshot :)

This Sprite was requested by Anorakun

name: smwsprites-any-sprite-generator
title: Any Sprite Generator
description:
A very customizable generator. It allows you to set which sprite to spawn (normal or custom, with support to up to 4 extra bytes for the latter), where in the screen the sprite can spawn and the speed it should spawn with (note that some sprites have hardcoded speeds or don't move).

All the settings are via the .asm file.

name: smwsprites-atomic-muncher
title: Atomic Muncher
description:
A muncher that will explode on ground contact. Includes fully custom behavior for the silver P-switch; that's why I wouldn't reccomend changing the graphics. The extra bit will determine the direction.

Note that you should replace the included GetDrawInfo, SubOffScreen, GetMap16 and ChangeMao16 with the ones we provided.

name: smwsprites-atomic-shroom-v1
title: Atomic Shroom v1.1
description:
This is a mushroom that explodes and shakes the ground if Mario touches it. Additionally, it can explode and flash after a certain amount of time to warn the player.

Look in the ASM file for configuration options.

Version 1.1 fixes two bugs that caused the sprite to continue to process even when offscreen, as well as when the sprites were locked. The .cfg has also been replaced with a JSON file and the sprite now uses Palette F by default.

name: smwsprites-auto-blast
title: Auto-Blast
description:
An invulnerable sprite that is inspired by the Auto-Bomb from Super Mario Bros. 2.

It moves around, blasting Bullet Bills at Mario at regular intervals. If the extra bit is set, it moves faster and occasionally jumps.

Check the ASM file for customization options.

name: smwsprites-baby-reznor-rotating-block
title: Baby Reznor + Rotating Block
description:
This includes:
1) a baby Reznor that shoots fireballs;
2) a rotating block that moves like the gray chained platforms, but otherwise behaves like a single-block Hammer Brother platform.
The two sprites can be used as standalone, but they also function in conjuction.


Regarding the baby Reznor, depending on the extra bit, it will either walk around occasionally facing the player, or attach to the included rotating block sprite. They take 3 fireballs to kill by default.

When attached to a rotating block, hitting it with a fireball will make it drop and start walking. When its block is hit from below, it can either drop and start walking, drop and start walking with 1 health point diminished or be killed. The last option is default, but this behavior can be changed in rotating_block.asm.


Regarding the rotating block, the extra bit determines its rotation direction, and with the extra bytes you can set its speed, radius and initial angle (rotating_block.asm describes some angle values you can use to place evenly spaced concentric platforms like those seen in the screenshots). Additionally, you can enable a functionality so the level exit activates once no baby Reznors are present in the level, effectively making these sprites work as a boss.


IMPORTANT! For both sprites to work in conjuction, they must be inserted in sequence in the sprite list like so (08 and 09 are just an example - they can be on any sequential pair of numbers):

08 baby_reznor.json
09 rotating_block.json

name: smwsprites-baby-yoshi
title: Baby Yoshi
description:
Disassembly of Baby Yoshi + added options for customization and glitch fixing.

Everything is explained in asm and text file included.

Make sure the extra property byte 2 is set to 80 (already like that in the json included).

Leave all the extra bytes to 00 for a vanilla green Baby Yoshi. First extra byte is the palette, check the files or in LM for options.

name: smwsprites-badges
title: Badges
description:
Formely known as "Hovering Items", those items can be picked up and they'll hover over player's head, giving some boost. Can be set to disappear on extra byte. More info is in ASM file.

Credit is optional.

name: smwsprites-bald-seahorse
title: Bald Seahorse
description: This seahorse, inspired in the ones at Wario Land, moves down and then up diagonally. When Mario gets into a customisable vertical and horizontal range, the seahorse starts to spin around after waiting some frames. If the seahorse collides with a wall while spinning, it will explode. Check the ASM file to customise this and more options.

name: smwsprites-ball-n-chain
title: Ball 'n Chain
description:
A disassembly of the Ball 'n Chain (sprite 9E), commented and ready to be inserted with PIXI. The extra bit controls the direction of rotation.

Now SA-1 hybrid.

name: smwsprites-balloon-gliders
title: Balloon Gliders
description:
Balloon Gliders will latch onto Mario and allow him to glide until the next time he jumps or Spin Jumps.

Included are two different functionings depending on the Extra bit. If clear, the Glider will have one balloon and make Mario glide downwards. If set, the glider will have 3 balloons and make Mario glide upwards.

This bug-fix also includes new features like an improved acceleration curve and the ability of going past the upwards speed limit (in case of springboard, note blocks, bouncing off enemies, etc).

Now SA-1 hybrid.

name: smwsprites-banana-peel
title: Banana Peel
description: A simple sprite that stuns the player when touched. If the extra bit is set, it will destroy itself after some frames.

name: smwsprites-bandit
title: Bandit
description:
These are the bandits from Yoshi's Island they can steal various items from the player such as Yoshi Coins, Regular Coins and 1ups. they also have extrabyte settings for what items they can't steal.

Give credit if used.

name: smwsprites-banzai-bill-v1
title: Banzai Bill v1.12
description:
This is a disassembly of sprite 9F in SMW, the Banzai Bill. I also made it able to go either direction if the extra bit is set (the original one doesn't show up at all when the player comes from the other direction). This sprite draws 16 tiles, so it requires the No Sprite Tile Limits patch; even sprite memory setting 04, which was used with the original Banzai Bill, doesn't seem to work.

1.1
----
Now compatible with pixi feature - 255 sprites per level

(Rykon-V73)Small change:

1.12
----
Added the option to edit tilemap and palette with ease.

1.13
You can also change the X speed and sound effect and its bank.

name: smwsprites-baron-von-zeppelin
title: Baron Von Zeppelin
description:
The little balloon from SMW2:YI which holds a configurable sprite. Green Needlenose is also included.

This sprite was part of smkdan's YI Pack 2, and was resubmitted separately after the remoderation for ease of search and to fit current standards.

DrAnas update: fixed two major oversights reported by MegaSonic1999 where the extra bit option for the Baron von Zeppelin to respawn after dropping its payload didn't actually work and running away from the Baron von Zeppelin after approaching it would permanently despawn it. Also, all previously-hardcoded sprite-related defines are now extra byte options!

- Extra byte 1 = How close Mario should get in order to drop payload.
- Extra byte 2 = carried sprite is custom or normal? - 0 = normal. 1 = custom.
- Extra byte 3 = carried sprite number.
- Extra byte 4 = 16x16 tile to use for the carried sprite.
- Extra byte 5 = tile properties for carried sprite, YXPPCCCT format.

name: smwsprites-base-bro-bomb-and-shell-bro-v1
title: Base Bro + Bomb and Shell Bro v1.0
description:
Bro sprite that throws a sprite.
What sprite is determined by the first extra property byte in the CFG editor and the tables inside the asm file.

Comes with Shell Bro and Bomb Bro.

v1.0
-----
Tattletale - moved out of pixi.

versions.title: Base Bro + Bomb and Shell Bro v1.0

name: smwsprites-baseball
title: Baseball
description: This is a disassembly of extended sprite 0D in SMW, Baseball.

name: smwsprites-basic-bounce-sprite
title: Basic Bounce Sprite
description:
Bounce block that turns into a solid invisible tile then an arbitrary Map16 tile.

Compatible with the SMB3 brick block from Custom Bounce Blocks 3.3

Requires Pixi 1.40 or later.

name: smwsprites-basilisk
title: Basilisk
description:
This sprite walks along the ground, trying to stay in front of Mario no matter what. It stands upright when not walking, and fires energy balls from its mouth at random intervals. It cannot be stomped, but 5 fireballs or a thrown item will kill it.

The energy balls from the included graphics replace baseballs.

Check the ASM file for customization options. The graphics for this sprite hail from Zelda II Adventure of Link.

Give credit if used or tweaked.

name: smwsprites-batadon
title: Batadon
description:
The winged totem-like creature from Super Mario Land that bounces and moves towards the player.

This sprite was part of smkdan's Super Mario Land sprites pack, and was resubmitted separately after the remoderation for ease of search and to fit current standards.

name: smwsprites-beet-platform
title: Beet Platform
description:
This platform will fall and slowly sink when in a fluid (lava/water). Credit Saturnyoshi as he drew the graphics and coded the SMBX original this sprite is inspired on.

(Rykon-V73)Small change: Fixed the .json file, since its original .json never has sprite tilemap and made the tilemap easier to edit.

name: smwsprites-beezo
title: Beezo
description:
This is the Beezo from SMB2.
By default, it contains 4 variations; 2 of which are not native to SMB2;
- Brown: Swoops down from the top left/right of the screen.
- Red: Moves straight.
- Green: Moves slowly and then quickly swoops down when the player passes by.
- Blue: Flies around the player's head, swooping down repeatedly before returning to its origin position and gives up after a few attempts.

Included is a generator which will automatically spawn Beezos at a regular interval.

Part of my SMB2 sprite standardization project; a project aiming to perfectly recreate the original enemies while adding new functionality.

Release History:
- 8/7/2023: V1.0 - Initial Release.

name: smwsprites-beezo-giant-beezo
title: Beezo + Giant Beezo
description:
The flying masked creature from SMB2 that flies straightforward like Eeries do, can be ridden on and be carried. Extra bit determines if it'll be a normal or a giant Beezo.

This sprite was part of mikeyk's SMB2 Updated sprites pack, and was resubmitted separately after the remoderation for ease of search and to fit current standards.

name: smwsprites-behind-net-spawner
title: Behind Net Spawner
description:
This sprite acts as a wrapper to spawn another sprite with the "behind scenery" (usually meant for nets, but comes up elsewhere) flag set. Sprites in this state won't interact with Mario unless he's also behind scenery (again, usually by using a net door).

A patch is included to make such sprites use priority 1 instead of the level default so they appear behind normal layer 1 tiles.

See the readme for instructions.

Requested by Theopold

name: smwsprites-better-bomb-koopa
title: Better Bomb Koopa
description: A koopa which explodes a certain time after being stomped. Insprited by mikeyk's, though this one is recoded from scratch and it represents a Koopa more accurately.

name: smwsprites-better-cheep-cheep
title: Better Cheep-Cheep
description:
changes
.EXGFX eliminates the discomfort of different colors.(If you using the original version, set it to yellow from the json file)
.Reverted the player's behavior when the fish is in the water to the default setting (which had a special behavior in the original). You can now spin jump off of a fish swimming in the surface and Yoshi can bounce off of it.
.Change swimming anime from frame-dependent to coordinate-dependent (this makes anime faster for fast individuals)
.The jumping height was changed from the pointer in the random number table to only a random number.
.Vertically moving fish always point in the direction of the player.
.The graphics are now always flipped vertically when defeated.
.Facing the player's direction when loading (including vertical)
.Add Sonikku's wet timer behavior.
.Can set the speed.
Requested by GooberFan75000

name: smwsprites-better-creating-eating-block-snakes
title: Better Creating/Eating Block Snakes
description:
This submission includes two sprites:
  • The improved Creating/Eating Block Snakes themselves
  • A custom "shooter", that spawns pairs of the main sprite

Both sprites are highly customizable and the paths are entirely determined by blocks you put in the level using Lunar Magic.
For this reason, this sprite includes a .map16 file with one row of blocks the sprite can interact with, namely:
  • turning left/right
  • turning either direction depending on the ON/OFF switch
  • changing speeds
  • terminating the snake

There's also a .dsc file that displays a description for the blocks in Lunar Magic, so you don't have to constantly reference the sprite's asm file to see what block does what.

Info on how to properly insert the blocks and the .dsc, along with lots of customization options, are in bettersnakes.asm.

name: smwsprites-better-dkc2-styled-skull-kart
title: Better DKC2-styled Skull Kart
description: A cart thing that moves automatically, similar to the one in DKC2. It has improved speed handling, uses more animation frames for going up/down slopes, as well as extra features - like slight accel and decceleration by pressing right or left.

name: smwsprites-better-pokey-v1
title: Better Pokey v1.1
description:
Improved Pokey from Super Mario World.

There are wall contact judgments throughout the head and torso.

It can be raised up to 16 steps including the head.
It is also possible to set whether or not to turn back at a step (note that opposed to a vanilla pokey, the yellow one stays on ledges, while the green one falls).

Fire and Cape are effective
If you come in contact with a baby yoshi, it will swallow your torso one piece at a time.
Attacking the head can also instantly knock it down..
It is possible to drop more than one torso at a time.

A thrown Goomba and Bob-omb are effective
Only works if X Speed is above a certain level.

Use Minor Extended Sprites for Pokey's segment.

You can set whether or not to follow a player.

-Update-
Enabled contact detection for MechaKoopa and sprites carried by the player. (See screenshot 8)
Fixed a bug where touching an object during cape flight would kill you regardless of whether it caused an ground pound or not.
New options for contact determination for extra sprites.
A setting has been added to hop when the Pokey is head-only.
A setting has been added to vary the X speed depending on the number of segments.

name: smwsprites-better-smb2-styled-pow
title: Better SMB2-styled POW
description:
A carryable POW switch similar to the one from SMB2. When triggered, and depending on a certain define in the ASM, it will either stun/kill sprites on ground like when you do a cape smash, or turn sprites on screen into coins, just like when you hit the goal tape in the end of a level.

The switch is carryable, too, and depending on the extra bit, you should either press it to trigger it or
throw it against something with a certain speed.

An optional ExAnimation file is also included, as well as a JSON file for PIXI 1.2 users.

Note that if carried through a pipe, it'll turn into a regular SMW blue POW, so you may want to avoid that.

name: smwsprites-betterer-boss-bass
title: Betterer Boss Bass
description:
The Boss Bass from Super Mario Bros. 3.

This sprite attempts to chase Mario down, and will jump and attempt to eat him. Being eaten is an instant-kill.

If the Extra Bit is set, it will be 16x16, and move slightly slower. It is unable to eat Mario at this point, but Mario can stomp it. This form uses the default Cheep Cheep graphics in SP3.

This sprite takes some code directly from Super Mario Bros. 3, so it's fairly accurate.

It's recommended that you use this with my Sprite Respawner sprite, as you can have the Boss Bass respawn whenever it gets killed.

Changelog:
4/17/2017: Won't eat Mario if he has Star power active.
8/31/2017: Converted to PIXI and added SA-1 support.

name: smwsprites-big-boo
title: Big Boo
description:
A disassembly of the Big Boo (sprite 28). It can always follow or follow when the player is facing it (Anti Boo behavior) depending on a define and when the extra bit is set.

Now SA-1 hybrid.

name: smwsprites-big-boo-boss
title: Big Boo Boss
description:
A custom sprite that's based on the original sprite. It circles around the screen and will trigger the settings once it has been defeated. Comes with:

-A normal Big Boo Boss config. (Triggers secret exit on extra bit)
-A Big Boo Boss config that changes into a door.

More details in the readme.

name: smwsprites-big-telly
title: Big Telly
description:
A large invulnerable sprite from Rockman and Forte. It moves towards Mario in a wave motion and occasionally stops to drop a 32x32 bomb which explodes on contact with the ground. Usage with the No More Sprite Tile Limits patch is recommended due to the fact the sprite draws 12 sprite tiles on screen, with the bomb taking up another 4.

Make sure to set the sprite number of the bomb (telly_bomb.cfg) in telly.asm! The readme contains additional information on the proper usage of this sprite.

name: smwsprites-big-timed-lift
title: Big Timed Lift
description:
This is a big 64x32 version of the Timed Lift (sprite BA), with some extra features. You can customize the timer between 1 and 255 seconds (or make it go on forever), set different movement types for each lift with different speeds, and more.

See the .asm file for customization options and details on using the extra bytes.

Replaces the Rex in GFX20 (SP4). No more sprite tile limits patch is strongly recommended (included in SA-1).

Requires the included CircleX and CircleY routines for the circle movement to work properly on LoROM when using large radii.

name: smwsprites-big-urchin
title: Big Urchin
description: This is a chunky child of God himself. Includes variations that rise from water, obey wall movement, move around depending on the X position or are just fixed in place.

name: smwsprites-bill-bomber
title: Bill Bomber
description:
This Bullet Bill throws Bob-ombs at Mario. If the extra bit is set, it will be a Bill Banzai, it will be invincible and it will throw 3 Bob-ombs at the same time.

(Rykon-V73): Small change: You can edit sound effects, tilemap, palettes and the contact routine.

name: smwsprites-bird-flies-after-contact
title: Bird, flies after contact
description:
This poor, shy lad will fly away when it comes in contact with either Mario or a sprite.
This is a C3 update. Now the birb animates correctly and gradually updates its speed instead of being a fixed static value.

name: smwsprites-birdfish
title: Birdfish
description:
This little guy from Super Mario Land 2 acts similarly to the vanilla jumping fish, but it always alternates one dive in water and one jump in the air. Additionally, it will hover for a bit when at the peak of the jump. Check out the asm file for configuration options such as speed, acceleration and hover time.
Included also a generator that acts similarly to the vanilla jumping fish generator.
Graphics provided by idol.

name: smwsprites-birdo
title: Birdo
description:
The miniboss creature from SMB2 that spits eggs and fireballs. Projectiles are included.

This sprite was part of mikeyk's SMB2 Updated sprites pack, and was resubmitted separately after the remoderation for ease of search and to fit current standards.

name: smwsprites-blargg
title: Blargg
description:
A disassembly of the Blargg (sprite A8), commented.

Now SA-1 hybrid.

name: smwsprites-blooper
title: Blooper
description:
A Blooper that acts like the SMB1 one. It can be stomped on when the player's outside water.

This sprite was part of Romi's Sprite Package, and was resubmitted separately after the remoderation for ease of search and to fit current standards.

Credit Romi for the original sprite.
No need to credit me.


UPDATE 16/07/2020: (Thiago678)
Made SA-1 hybrid.

name: smwsprites-blooper-nanny
title: Blooper Nanny
description: A Blooper Nanny seen in many underwater levels of SMB3. It is the Blooper with four smaller Bloopers following it.

name: smwsprites-blue-boomerang-boomerang-bros
title: Blue Boomerang / Boomerang Bros.
description:
The Blue Boomerang from Super Mario Advance 4's e-Reader levels.

It can be picked up and thrown, and it will kill enemies in a similar way to a thrown shell. It cannot be thrown up or placed back down once it's been picked up.

Additionally, it includes an updated Boomerang Bros. sprite which will throw a new Extended Sprite -- it functions similarly to the existing sprite, but it will turn into the carriable Blue Boomerang once the Boomerang Bros. that threw it is defeated.

If you're using my other Boomerang Bros. sprite, you can replace it with this version and it should work without issue.

name: smwsprites-blue-parakoopa-flies-in-a-circle
title: Blue Parakoopa, Flies in a Circle
description:
A complete remake of my old blue Parakoopa, itself inspired by Alcaro's removed sprite.
This is a parakoopa which flies in a circle pattern. The extra bit controls the rotation. The first extension byte controls the radius of the parakoopa; values between 01 and 7F are recommended.

versions.title: Blue Parakoopa, Flies in a Circle

name: smwsprites-blurp-fish
title: Blurp Fish
description:
This is a disassembly of the blurp fish, it's ready to be inserted with PIXI.

Credit is not necessary but would be nice as I spent along time doing this.

name: smwsprites-bob-omb
title: Bob-omb
description: A disassembly of sprite 0D, the Bob-omb. Unlike the old one, this recreates the entirety of states of the vanilla Bob-omb, making it more accurate, not depend on bypassing the sprite status with the second extra property byte, and allowing you to customize stuff related to its carriable form.

name: smwsprites-bob-omb-leaves-fire-trail
title: Bob-omb, Leaves Fire Trail
description:
A Bob-omb which leaves a fire trail every certain amount of time, controlled by the fourth extra byte.

Requested by Green during C3 Winter 2025. That one used the old, now-removed Bob-omb disassembly. This one uses my own disassembly as a base, now with X speed, time before being quiet, and time before exploding all parametrized in extra bytes.

name: smwsprites-bob-omb-shooter
title: Bob-omb Shooter
description:
bobomb shooter from smb3
requested by Xulon

name: smwsprites-bob-omb-tower
title: Bob-omb Tower
description:
A tower of 4 Bob-ombs that walks towards Mario. If jumped on the bombs all drop to the ground ready to explode. Based on Goomba Tower by Darolac.

Bob-omb state and explosion timer can be configured in the sprite's code. Can also be configured to use a custom bomb.

name: smwsprites-boingboingsplat
title: Boingboingsplat
description:
A small blue blob that bounces up and down in one spot, over and over and over. If he's placed on an incline, he'll bounce down it instead. Fireballs won't hurt him.

This sprite was originally part of andy_k_250's Custom Tweaked Sprites pack, and was resubmitted separately after the remoderation for ease of search and to fit current standards. They were made as a demo of the ability for mikeyk's Spritetool (also inherited by PIXI) to create tweaked copies of vanilla sprites without altering the vanilla sprites themselves, via a .cfg file that does not reference an .asm file at all. Therefore, the lack of .asm files in this download is not only intentional, it is the main idea.

name: smwsprites-bomb
title: Bomb
description:
It's a bomb sprite from Sprite Tool, converted and ready to be inserted with PIXI.
It falls straight down and explodes when it touches the ground. It's better used in conjunction with custom shooters, generators and other sprites.

name: smwsprites-bomb-football
title: Bomb Football
description:
This is a football that explodes like a bob-omb.

Credit is unecessary.

name: smwsprites-bombable-block-sprite
title: Bombable Block Sprite
description:
This is a sprite that is solid and can be destroyed only by explosion.

Credit is unecessary. This is a remake of Dispari Scuro's rejected "Bob-omb Block" sprite, and includes graphics from said submission.

name: smwsprites-bomber
title: Bomber
description:
This is Bomber from Kirby series. This enemy walks like normal, until it finds a ledge end, after which it'll balance for a short time, then it'll fall down and explode when it lands. On extra bit set, it'll generate a bigger explosion.

Requested by NopeContest.

name: smwsprites-bone-pile
title: Bone Pile
description: A pile of bones that simply stays wherever you put it. If the player gets close, the sprite transforms into the original Dry Bones (ones that walk around or throw bones depending on the initial X position of the sprite). No credit needed. Made on Lynnes' request.

name: smwsprites-bonus-game-claw-machine
title: Bonus Game - Claw Machine
description:
This sprite is, effectively, a new bonus game meant to act as a replacement to the one found in Level 000/100. With the Bonus Game Destination Expander patch, you can also use it in conjunction with the default bonus game, or any others.

Modeled after Super Mario Land 2's bonus game but drawn to fit a style reminiscent of SMW/SMM2, this bonus game is intended to be a unique challenge for players. An assortment of 8 items are created at random (from multiple sets of item pools which may be customized) and move along the conveyor belt.
Stepping on the blue switch will cause the claw to descend, grabbing any item that happens to be at that position.
With the default settings, the claw inverts direction and speeds up after each try. Both of these behaviors can of course be disabled.

Several items can spawn which will give the player more tries, re-rolls all available items, or a Bob-Omb which destroys the crane and ends the minigame. A skilled player can keep playing so long as they they aim to refresh their tries and the items on the conveyor.

An example level making use of this sprite (in the list.txt slot of 00) is included, to give an example of the preferred way to set the room up.

Disclaimer: It's suggested to use the sprite alongside NMSTL or SA-1. Moreover, it should only be inserted once in the first screen of a single screen horizontal level, otherwise it will glitch.

name: smwsprites-bonus-star
title: Bonus Star
description: This is a small, simple star sprite (graphics from Yoshi's Island) that bounces around and gives you bonus stars depending on the extra property bytes.  Credit is not necessary unless you want to; this took me only about 5-10 minutes to make.

name: smwsprites-bony-beetle
title: Bony Beetle
description:
This is a disassembly of the bony beetle - sprite 31 - from the original game.

Update:
-SA-1 compatible
-Removed redutant code that caused it to sometimes face away from player

name: smwsprites-boo
title: Boo
description:
A disassembly of the Boo (sprite 37). It can always follow or follow when the player is facing it (Anti Boo behavior) depending on a define and when the extra bit is set.

Now SA-1 hybrid.

name: smwsprites-boo-block
title: Boo Block
description:
This is a disassembly of SMW's Boo Block. Half of it is commented. Graphics routine was coded by me, not disassembled. Palette is hardcoded - go into the .asm file to change it. (I commented it.) Credit not needed.

Now SA-1 hybrid.

name: smwsprites-boo-ring
title: Boo Ring
description:
This is a custom sprite version of the Boo Ring. It is more efficient than the vanilla version and quite customizable.

You can set the number of Boos, space between each Boo, radius, speed, and rotation direction for every instance of the sprite. The rotation direction is controlled by the extra bit (clockwise if clear, counter-clockwise if set). The sprite uses all four extra bytes (the extension field in Lunar Magic's "Add Sprite Manual" dialog) to control, in order, the number of Boos, the space between each Boo, the radius, and the speed. An extension of 0A285010 (10 Boos, $28 pixels between each Boo, a radius of 5 tiles = $50 pixels, a speed of $10) replicates the vanilla Boo Ring.

The No More Sprite Tile Limits patch is required if you want to use this sprite.

Note for advanced hackers: This sprite uses the WRAM write registers ($2180-$2183) for its OAM transfer. If you use these registers during an interrupt, there might be a crash. If you don't know what this means, you probably don't have to worry about it.

2017/09/07 Update
- Merged the normal and SA-1 versions.
- Made the sprite use extra bytes instead of define and extra property bytes for its options.

2016/06/14 Update
- Fixed to turn in the correct direction. (BooRing.asm)
- More optimized. (all sprites)

name: smwsprites-boo-stream
title: Boo Stream
description:
A disassembly of the reflecting Boo stream (sprite B0), commented.

Now SA-1 hybrid.

name: smwsprites-boo-stream-tail
title: Boo Stream Tail
description:
Disassembly of the Boo Stream Tail, the minor extended sprite that the Boo Stream spawns.

Extracted from Thomas' all.log. Requires pixi 1.40 or later.

name: smwsprites-boogie-beta-sprite
title: Boogie (Beta Sprite)
description:
An interpretation of a scrapped beta sprite, popularly known as Boogie (seen in chr-stock-2-minidragon.OBJ).

This funny little man dances in place wherever he's placed in the level. If approached by the player, a player's fireball, a Yoshi fireball, or a thrown sprite, Boogie will teleport, reappearing elsewhere after a bit like a Magikoopa. Do note that Boogie won't follow the player around like a Magikoopa, though.

If the Extra Bit is set, Boogie will launch a projectile at the player upon reappearing.

This submission includes UberASM code that, if enabled, allows all active Boogie sprites to perform a special synchronized dance that can conjure a variety of customizable effects, from flipping the ON/OFF flag to killing the player. Both this function and the sprite itself are highly customizable, see the .asm files for more details.

name: smwsprites-boom-guy
title: Boom Guy
description: This is the Boom Guy, based off of the one from M&LPiT. It's a Shyguy that walks around, shooting Bullet Bills with its cannon. When it's about to die, it loses its cannon and tries to flee.

name: smwsprites-boomerang-bro
title: Boomerang Bro
description:
A Boomerang Bro from Super Mario Bros. 3. It walks back and forth, occasionally hopping and periodically throwing two boomerangs, which it will later try to catch.

It throws an extended sprite boomerang. The included ExtendedGetDrawInfo fixes a crash in PIXI's, so it is highly recommended you replace it with it.

Make sure to specify the extended sprite number of the boomerang (extended/boomerang.asm) from list.txt in the Boomerang Bro's ASM file (sprites/BoomerangBro.asm)!

Mod edit 2025-2-9: Fixed a typo in the boomerang tilemap resulting in some garbled graphics, reported by Atari2.0

name: smwsprites-boomerang-bro-v1
title: Boomerang Bro v1.0
description:
Similar to his role in SMB3, this guy throws boomerangs at Mario.

BIG FAT NOTE: This sprite depends on the boomerang sprite. Make sure you insert the boomerang as the very next sprite. (ex. If this is sprite 1B, make the boomerang 1C).

Uses first extra bit: NO

Comes with the boomerang sprite

v1.0
-----
Tattletale - moved out of pixi.

name: smwsprites-boomerang-dry-bones
title: Boomerang Dry Bones
description:
This Dry Bones throws bones that move like a boomerang.

Requested by Anorakun.

name: smwsprites-boost-platform
title: Boost Platform
description:
Jumps up when Mario steps off the platform. Can be stood on in midair and jumped off of again.

6 cfg files are included:
- boost_plat_2tiles.cfg
- boost_plat_3tiles.cfg
- boost_plat_4tiles.cfg
^ Can only jump from their starting position.

- boost_plat_2tiles_gold.cfg
- boost_plat_3tiles_gold.cfg
- boost_plat_4tiles_gold.cfg
^ Jump off whenever Mario steps off, even when in the air.

Now PIXI compatible.

name: smwsprites-bopping-toady-v1
title: Bopping Toady v1.0
description:
This is a simple sprite that moves only by jumping. It can attack by extending its tongue. Its interaction is very standard. It has an option for using an alternate palette underwater, which might be useful if you want it to look more blue or something like that.

Requested for the Strongest Sprite Workshop 2020 by Yoshin.

name: smwsprites-boss-fireball
title: Boss Fireball
description:
This is a disassembly of sprite 34 in SMW, the boss fireball (spat by Ludwig).
NOTE: This sprite behaves exactly like original sprite 34, meaning it is stationary unless its X speed is set by another sprite when it is spawned.

name: smwsprites-bouncing-boo-stream
title: Bouncing Boo Stream
description: This is a boo stream that has gravity and bounces off the ground.

name: smwsprites-bouncing-cannonball
title: Bouncing Cannonball
description:
Cannonballs are heavy metal spheres that are normally launched from cannons at high speeds, but this kind is so anxious to be fired out of a cannon that it jumps around nervously until its turn comes.

This sprite was originally part of andy_k_250's Custom Tweaked Sprites pack, and was resubmitted separately after the remoderation for ease of search and to fit current standards. They were made as a demo of the ability for mikeyk's Spritetool (also inherited by PIXI) to create tweaked copies of vanilla sprites without altering the vanilla sprites themselves, via a .cfg file that does not reference an .asm file at all. Therefore, the lack of .asm files in this download is not only intentional, it is the main idea.

name: smwsprites-bouncing-football
title: Bouncing Football
description: A disassembly of the bouncing football (sprite 1B), ready to be inserted with PIXI.

name: smwsprites-bouncing-paraspiny
title: Bouncing Paraspiny
description:
A merge of the Spiny and the green bouncing Parakoopa. You can control the jump height with the extra bit.

Remember that spin jumping on rapidly rising spiky enemies is not recommended.

name: smwsprites-bouncing-power-thwomp-thwimp
title: Bouncing Power Thwomp/Thwimp
description:
This is Thwomp/Thwimp that bounces up 'n down and stun player when he/she's on ground.

Originally from Thwomp pack by yoshicookiezeus.

name: smwsprites-bouncing-rex
title: Bouncing Rex
description: This is a Rex that bounces around like the bouncing Parakoopa. The extra bit determines its bouncing height.

name: smwsprites-bouncing-spiky-ball
title: Bouncing Spiky Ball
description:
Made out of boredom and to test my limited spriting skills.

This is basically a spiked ball that hops up and down while following Mario. Speeds and tilemap are easily customizable.

name: smwsprites-bouncing-spiny-egg
title: Bouncing Spiny Egg
description:
Bouncing Spiny Egg. Comes with cleaner code and slower movement to improve usability.

It bounces off slopes at predetermined angles based on steepness. Also bounces off walls and rides along the ceiling until it falls.

Now PIXI compatible.

(Rykon-V73)Small change: Added .json file and made the tilemap easier to edit.

name: smwsprites-bouncing-spiny-egg-rolling-spiny-egg
title: Bouncing Spiny Egg + Rolling Spiny Egg
description:
Bouncing Spiny Egg will bounce off the ground slopes at a strict angle. (Set Extra bits to 2)
Rolling Spiny Egg will pick up speed if placed on a slope and even decelerate and go the other way. (Set Extra bits to 3)

There's a bunch more that can be done with this, but that's the gist of it.

Update March 9th 2017: Horizontal Speed adjustments for the bouncing spinies! They will bounce off slope with half the speed they did before in order to facilitate level design. As such, the screenshots depicting them are no longer accurate until I update those as well. Sorry for the inconvenience!

versions.title: Bouncing Spiny Egg + Rolling Spiny Egg

name: smwsprites-bouncy-boo
title: Bouncy Boo
description:
This Boo bounces around, like a Puntin' Chuck football or a Diggin' Chuck rock. You can make it bounce always, or only when not stared at.

Dedicated to Boosius, I wouldn't be able to come up with something like this myself lol.

name: smwsprites-bouncy-cloud
title: Bouncy Cloud
description: A cloud you can bounce off, based off NSMBWii's bouncy clouds. You'll bounce higher when holding A or B. The heights (Y speeds for the player) as well as the sound effects can be configured in the .asm file.

name: smwsprites-bowling-goonie
title: Bowling Goonie
description:
The fat rolling bird from Yoshi's Island. Note that this sprite doesn't work well with slopes.

Originally from smkdan's Yoshi's Island dynamic sprite pack.

name: smwsprites-bowser
title: Bowser
description: A Bowser from Romi's Sprite Tool, converted and ready to be inserted with PIXI.

name: smwsprites-bowser-blade
title: Bowser Blade
description:
This sprite is a giant blade inspired in the ones on Yoshi's Story that moves around and damages in contact. If the extra bit is set, the blade will be upside down.

You can customise the tiles used by the sprite in the ASM file.

(Small change by Rykon-V73): You can now also customise the horizontal speed, whether the sprite hurts or kills the player and add some sound effects.

name: smwsprites-bowser-fire
title: Bowser Fire
description: A fire that jumps. Mario can't jump nor spinjump on him without taking damage. You can customize the height of the jump from the asm file. That's about it.

name: smwsprites-bowser-fist
title: Bowser Fist
description:
This is a giant fist inspired in the ones at Super Mario Land 2: Six Golden Coins that moves up and down once a certain block is pressed. That block (trap.asm, included with this sprite) must be inserted a block inserter and sets up a freeRAM flag when the player is above it, efectively activating this sprite.

IMPORTANT:

You will have to tell the sprite which free RAM is the block using. To do that, just write the RAM adress you are using as free RAM in the extension field of the insert sprite window in Lunar Magic using the two first extra bytes (for example, if you are going to use $58 as your free RAM, just write 0058). The sprite assumes that the RAM is in the $7E bank, so you will be restricted to that bank.

name: smwsprites-bowser-statue
title: Bowser Statue
description:
This is a disassembly of the Bowser statue. (Yes, it's the actual statue this time, not just the fireball.) I'd always thought the Bowser statue was one of the coolest sprites in SMW, so I wanted to disassemble it. I did have to change the code a bit, though...the original flame-spitting routine didn't work, and I never figured out why. I included both my modified version and the original code ripped straight from all.log.

This ZIP also features a custom version whose behaviour is controlled by extra bytes rather than X position and also has the ability to do both, jump and shoot fireballs.

name: smwsprites-bowser-statue-fireball
title: Bowser Statue Fireball
description: This is a disassembly of the fireball that the Bowser statues spit. If you use it, don't bother to credit me, but if you base another sprite off of it, I would appreciate some credit.

name: smwsprites-bronto-burt
title: Bronto Burt
description:
The Bronto Burt from Kirby, a 16x16 sprite which flies in a straight line. If it's put on the ground, it will wait for Mario to come close to it before taking off.

Originally part of the Kirby Sprite Pack.

name: smwsprites-brown-block-bridge
title: Brown Block Bridge
description:
This bridge is made out of brown blocks, which turn into coins when the blue P-Switch is active.
Note that due to the amount of processing time this sprite takes, SA-1 may be needed for a better experience.

name: smwsprites-brown-checkerboard-line-guided-platform-v1
title: Brown/Checkerboard Line-Guided Platform v1.1
description:
This is a disassembly of sprite 63 in SMW, the brown/checkerboard line-guided platform. The extra bit determines which tilemap and interaction size it will use.

Now SA-1 hybrid.

v1.1
-----
Support for LM3 exlevel settings. Only works with pixi 1.2.4+

title: Brown Line-Guided Platform v1.1

This is a disassembly of sprite 62 in SMW, the brown line-guided platform.

Now SA-1 hybrid.

v1.1
-----
Support for LM3 exlevel settings. Only works with pixi 1.2.4+

name: smwsprites-bubble-with-instant-explosive
title: Bubble with Instant Explosive
description: This is a bubble that carries a bomb that explodes instantly when bubble pops.

name: smwsprites-bubble-with-sprite-inside
title: Bubble With Sprite Inside
description:
A disassembly of sprite 9D, the flying bubble with a sprite inside.

It comes with some customization options as well as CFG files for the sprites that can be inside the bubble, so you are no longer dependant on X-Positions.

name: smwsprites-bucket-head
title: Bucket Head
description:
Enclosed is a Bucket Head and snowflakes.

The Bucket Head shoots snowflakes at Mario, that can freeze him or damage him (Or both). The Snowflake Sprite must be inserted as the very next Sprite.

ExGFX included.

name: smwsprites-bullet-bill
title: Bullet Bill
description:
This is a disassembly of sprite 1C in SMW, the Bullet Bill.

Setting the extra bit makes the bullet bill play a sound effect and don't go behind the scenes.

Minor update 2023-03-03: updated a quasi-broken .json file in the zip.

name: smwsprites-bullet-bill-generator
title: Bullet Bill Generator
description:
This is a disassembly of sprite D5 in SMW, Bullet Bill Generator.
Credit is unnecessary.

name: smwsprites-bully
title: Bully
description:
This is Bully, as seen in SM64. When the player touches it, they get bumped. Extra bit determines if it'll be a small or a big Bully.

This sprite was part of Romi's Sprite Package, and was resubmitted separately after the remoderation for ease of search and to fit current standards.

name: smwsprites-bumper-v1
title: Bumper v1.1
description:
This is a simple 32x32 sprite that bounces the player away when touched. It can either be stationary or line guided depending on Extra Byte 1, and if line-guided, can move at different speeds. For how to set this, read the Readme/ASM file.

The sprite also includes defines for tilemap, bounce speeds, SFX for bouncing and how long to animate the bumper after bouncing the player.

Sprite is compatible with Line Guide Acts-Like Fix patch.

v1.1
-----
Support for LM3 exlevel settings. Only works with pixi 1.2.4+

name: smwsprites-bumpty
title: Bumpty
description:
The penguin from SMW2:YI. When touched, Bumpty will bump the player.

This sprite was part of Romi's Sprite Package, and was resubmitted separately after the remoderation for ease of search and to fit current standards.

Darolac's edit: changed the order of a LDX and changed a bit a properties table to fix a lot of graphical bugs with the hand and leg tiles.

name: smwsprites-bunbun
title: Bunbun
description:
The bee-like creature from Super Mario Land that drops little stakes every once in a while.

This sprite was part of smkdan's Super Mario Land sprites pack, and was resubmitted separately after the remoderation for ease of search and to fit current standards.

name: smwsprites-buster-beetle
title: Buster Beetle
description:
The Buster Beetle from Super Mario Bros. 3. It will walk (falling off ledges). It will pick up any Throw Blocks in its way and throw them at Mario in attempt to hurt him. Any attack can defeat it.

Make sure to specify the sprite number (from list.txt) of the block (buster_block.cfg) in buster.asm! Check the ASM files for customization options.

name: smwsprites-buzz-bomber-v1
title: Buzz Bomber v1.0
description:
This Sonic-inspired sprite will fly in and unleash its ammo in the form of fireballs. How much ammo it has without and with the extra bit can be very easily changed in the defines. The sprite is very simple and has pretty standard interaction.

Requested for the Strongest Sprite Workshop 2020 by Green Jerry

name: smwsprites-candle-flames-in-background
title: Candle Flames in Background
description:
This is a disassembly of sprite E6 in SMW, Candle flames in background.

Credit is unecessary.

name: smwsprites-cannonball
title: Cannonball
description:
This is a combination of a standard sprite and shooter.

The sprite itself is originally designed for use in other sprites as a projectile, or shot from shooter sprites in Airship-like levels.

Functionally, it is similar to a Bullet Bill. However, it comes with added functionality -- such as being able to collide with walls (bouncing harmlessly off of them), exploding on contact with walls/the player/other sprites, and so on.

The shooter has a few configurations that it comes with by default -- shooting in 8 directions, or left/right or up/down based on the player's position.

The preview GIF has the !ShotzoJitter option enabled in the sprite's ASM file. This produces an effect similar to bullets in the Kirby series.

Two JSON files are included for both the sprite and the shooter. The ones ending in "_PIXI1.40" are intended for PIXI v1.40. If you are using PIXI v1.32, use the standard JSON files or you'll run into insertion errors.

Note: If using as a projectile within another publicly-released custom sprite, please do so without renaming it, and link this submission's page, as this sprite may be updated to include added functionality down the line.

name: smwsprites-carriable-goal-point-question-sphere
title: Carriable Goal Point Question Sphere
description:
A goal sphere which can be carried. To trigger the goal sequence, approach it without pressing X or Y.

With the extra byte, the exit triggered (normal or secret 1, 2 or 3) can be selected, and the glitter can be toggled.

name: smwsprites-carriable-reusable-p-switch-stump
title: Carriable Reusable P-Switch Stump
description:
A P-Switch stump which can be re-activated with a block.
Two blocks are included:
1. A basic block which just re-activates every stump it touches.
2. A more powerful block which can be triggered by the player, other sprites, cape and fire, and which can trigger only one or all stumps of either one color or both colors. It can also change into another Map16 tile and it includes an optional bounce sprite.

Requested by 3dsalmon.

name: smwsprites-carrot-top-lifts
title: Carrot Top Lifts
description: This is a disassembly of the Carrot Top Lifts, sprites B7 and B8. The extra bit determines which of the original sprites it acts like.

versions.title: Carrot Top Lifts
versions.filename: SMWSDIS - sprites B7 %26 B8 - Carrot Top Lifts.zip

name: smwsprites-carryable-dry-bones
title: Carryable Dry Bones
description:
This is a Dry Bones that can be carried by the player after collapsing.

Requested by Knetog during Winter C3 2023.

name: smwsprites-carryable-football
title: Carryable Football
description:
This is a football that player can carry around and use it as deadly weapon of poor randomness against enemies. It can also explode on enemy contact and hit blocks.

Please give credit if used.

name: smwsprites-carryable-pipe
title: Carryable Pipe
description:
This sprite is used in pairs. You can carry them around, and when you enter one of them, like a pipe, you'll be teleported to the other end.

You can have up to four different pairs in a level at the same time, which act independently of each other and are distinguished by their color. The pairing depends on the extra byte.

A pair of pipes only works when there are exactly two of them in the level, and both are spawned (=the player has encountered both); they won't let you enter otherwise.

name: smwsprites-carryable-sprite-killer-v1
title: Carryable Sprite Killer v1.1
description:
This sprite is a sphere that can be picked up and carried around, and will indiscriminately destroy (almost) any sprite it comes into contact with. It can be set to destroy an unlimited number of sprites, or you can set it to self-destruct after destroying a specified number of sprites via extra byte 1. You can also set a "self-destruct" timer which will start counting down after killing the first sprite, and you can select which palette row the Sprite Killer uses with extra byte 3.
Includes a basic "death sphere" graphic that overwrites half the Hammer Bro in GFX13 (SP3).

Requested by Earthling.

v1.1 (18/01/2021):
- Now uses a vanilla interaction routine which allows the Sprite Killer to account for sprites of different hitbox sizes.
- Added a "self-destruct timer" feature, which is set by extra byte 2.
- Added an "exclusion" feature: You can define vanilla and custom sprites to be excluded from being killed, by adding their number to exclusion tables in the .asm file.
- Moved the palette option to extra byte 3.
- Redesigned the graphic.

name: smwsprites-carryable-yoshi-s-island-p-switch
title: Carryable Yoshi's Island P-Switch
description:
This is a large P-Switch from Yoshi's Island. Unlike original, the player can carry or move it somehow.

Credit is optional. Requested by gui.

name: smwsprites-castle-candle-flame
title: Castle Candle Flame
description:
This is a disassembly of cluster sprite 05 in SMW, Castle candle flame.

Credit is unecessary.

name: smwsprites-cave-in-generator
title: Cave-In Generator
description:
A generator which will shake the screen and randomly spawn 16x16 or 32x32 blocks which will fall down. They can optionally hurt Mario.

This version uses cluster sprites for the blocks, which means they won't take up standard sprite slots and will cause way less slowdown.You can find the standard sprite version here.

Make sure to set the cluster sprite number of the block (cluster/caveinblock.asm) in the generator's ASM file (generators/caveingen.asm)! Use the number from list.txt.

Check the ASM files for customization options. By default, the blocks will treat all Map16 tiles on page 1 (and ones which act like them) as solid. Note that the blocks don't interact with layer 2.

name: smwsprites-cave-story-basil
title: Cave Story - Basil
description:
The moving fire that appears in the Egg Corridor level from Cave Story.
The Extra bit determines whether it kills or just hurt Mario. You can also configure the distance that if is higher, basil changes its direction.
DOES NOT WORK WITH SLOPES. USE ON PLANE SURFACE.

Now SA-1 hybrid.

name: smwsprites-cave-story-beetle
title: Cave Story - Beetle
description:
The beetle from Egg Corridor in Cave Story, this is the one that moves between two walls.

It cannot be jumped on normally, and must be placed on the right extremity of the area in which it'll move.

More info in the readme. Also includes a readme in spanish.

name: smwsprites-cave-story-mannon
title: Cave Story - Mannon
description:
The tomb that appears in Grass Town level from Cave Story.
Graphics, palette and the projectile that it shoots included. Extra bit controls FIXED direction.
Give credits if used.

The error in the CFG is fixed now.

Now SA-1 hybrid.

name: smwsprites-ceiling-buzzy-beetle
title: Ceiling Buzzy Beetle
description:
A Buzzy Beetle that walks on the ceiling and drops when you get underneath.

Tester's note: Make sure to block him off, or else he'll start scuttling on air.

name: smwsprites-ceiling-thwimp
title: Ceiling Thwimp
description:
It's Thwimp, except he falls upwards and swoops down from the ceiling.

Now PIXI compatible.

name: smwsprites-celeste-controllable-platform
title: Celeste - Controllable Platform
description:
This platform will move in a direction in an horizontal or vertical manner automatically, with the player being able to control how it moves in the opposite axis. See the ASM file for more information.
Note that this requires a patch (that will be installed when you insert the sprite) to be able to use the respawning feature.

v1.1
* Updated for PIXI.
* Somewhat fixed SA-1 conversion (but untested anyways so I'm not putting the tag.

name: smwsprites-chainless-chomp-and-parachomp
title: Chainless Chomp and Parachomp
description:
These are Chain Chomps on the loose, with Parachomps additionally having small stubby wings that allow them to bounce around and hover. They can only be stopped if Mario runs into them while invincible.

This sprite was originally part of andy_k_250's Custom Tweaked Sprites pack, and was resubmitted separately after the remoderation for ease of search and to fit current standards. They were made as a demo of the ability for mikeyk's Spritetool (also inherited by PIXI) to create tweaked copies of vanilla sprites without altering the vanilla sprites themselves, via a .cfg file that does not reference an .asm file at all. Therefore, the lack of .asm files in this download is not only intentional, it is the main idea.

name: smwsprites-chainsaws-v-1
title: Chainsaws v.1.2
description:
This is a disassembly of sprites 65 and 66 in SMW, the chainsaws. The extra bit determines which of the original sprites it acts like.

v1.2
-----
CFG for property byte 1. Fixed cfg act-as.

v1.1
-----
Support for LM3 exlevel settings. Only works with pixi 1.2.4+
SA-1 compliant now.

name: smwsprites-chargin-chuck
title: Chargin' Chuck
description:
MikeyK's disassembly of Chargin' Chuck from Super Mario World

Setting the extra bit gives it infinite HP, meaning you can jump on it endlessly.

name: smwsprites-charging-spiny
title: Charging Spiny
description:
This sprite acts like a normal SMB3 Spiny, but when Mario comes near it, it retreats into its shell and dashes towards him after spinning in place for a short amount of time.

Check the ASM file for customization options.

name: smwsprites-chasing-boo-stream
title: Chasing Boo Stream
description:
This boo stream chases the player.

Update 25.09.2024:
-Made use of extra bytes for max speed and acceleration.
-Fixed the sprite clipping through objects when !ObjInt was enabled.

name: smwsprites-chasing-explosive-swooper
title: Chasing (Explosive) Swooper
description:
A swooper that chases after player after being disturbed. Includes an explosive variant that explodes after a little while.

Requested by Roberto zampari and SF - The Dark Warrior during Winter C3 2023.

name: smwsprites-chasing-hidden-rex
title: Chasing & Hidden Rex
description:
This is a Rex that chases you, like Disco Shell. In fact, it can be set to flash and become invulnerable to stomps.
It can also be set to remain "hidden" untill player comes close.

No GIEPY support this time, sorry.

Requested by Roberto zampari, zacmario and Blizzard Buffalo.

name: smwsprites-chasing-mega-mole
title: Chasing Mega Mole
description:
A Mega Mole that chases the player. It'll continue moving in the same direction if stood on.

Requested by Klug during Summer C3 2023.

name: smwsprites-chasing-ninji
title: Chasing Ninji
description:
An edit of the Thwimp disassembly to make it act like a Ninji which follows you. Demonstration video: http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UGVnBxf8QR0

Credit is appreciated but isn't necessary.

Now SA-1 hybrid.

name: smwsprites-chasing-porcupuffer
title: Chasing Porcupuffer
description: This porcupuffer will follow Mario even underwater. It doesn't move along layer 1 as the original porcupuffer does, and it's also customisable regarding its speed and acceleration - you can also decide if you want it to despawn offscreen or not. Check the .asm file regarding those options.

name: smwsprites-chasing-urchin-shoots-fire
title: Chasing Urchin, Shoots Fire
description:
This Urchin will chase the player and shoot fireballs. As strange as it sounds.
Requested by Samantha.

name: smwsprites-checkerboard-platforms
title: Checkerboard Platforms
description: This is a disassembly of sprites 55 and 57 in Super Mario World, the checkerboard platforms which move horizontally and vertically. The extra bit determines which of the original two sprites it acts like.

name: smwsprites-cheep-cheep-that-moves-like-a-dolphin
title: Cheep-Cheep that moves like a dolphin
description:
A cheep-cheep that follows a pattern similar to an original game dolphin. The extra bit will set the pattern it follows. Requires sprite buoyancy to be enabled.
Requested by Blind Devil.

versions.title: Cheep-Cheep that moves like a dolphin

name: smwsprites-chucks
title: Chucks
description: This is a disassembly of all Chuck sprites in Super Mario World, which are sprites 46 and 91 through 98, which are Diggin', Chargin', Splittin', Bouncin', Whistlin', Clappin', Duplicate Chargin', Puntin' and Pitchin' Chucks, respectively.

name: smwsprites-chuckya
title: Chuckya
description: This is that SM64 sprite that resembles a giant purple Bob-Omb that can pick Mario up and throw him into the distance. (Mario can kill him by using the same method) Since it is dynamic, you will have to install dsx.asm. No credit needed.

name: smwsprites-circling-thwomp
title: Circling Thwomp
description:
This thwomp will change it's direction every time it hits the ground.

Extra bit will make it go counter-clockwise

Requested by Ruberjig

name: smwsprites-classic-goomba-and-bouncing-paragoomba-v1
title: Classic Goomba and Bouncing Paragoomba v1.2
description: This is a stompable Goomba/Paragoomba that behaves like in SMB3. Extra bit determines if it'll be a regular Goomba or a Bouncing Paragoomba. Includes a define in the ASM file which allows you to use a separate palette for both variations or not.

versions.title: Classic Goomba and Bouncing Paragoomba v1.2

name: smwsprites-clawgrip
title: Clawgrip
description:
Clawgrip from SMB2.

Has numerous capabilities as far as customization goes; how fast it moves or throws rocks, how many times it goes back and forth or how many rocks it throws, as well as the ability for it to have multiple phases.

The code is loosely based on the SMB2 code itself but then heavily adapted, so the default pattern of the thrown rocks is almost identical and as such the same arena layout can be utilized.

Released as part of C3 2022.

Release History:
-- 7/10/2022 (v1.0) - Initial release.

name: smwsprites-claymore
title: Claymore
description:
This is a claymore mine that will explode when Mario or another sprite trips the laser. It has a wide range of customization options that can allow it to be picked up and thrown around to function like a tool for Mario, or make it a deadly enemy that must be avoided at all costs.

You can change the claymore's detection range, the trip timer, the explosion length, and many other behaviours. All settings are controlled by the extra bytes, for which you can find details in the asm file.

name: smwsprites-clear-dry-bones
title: Clear Dry Bones
description:
A variation of a Dry Bone which intangible (can't be attacked and — depending on the settings — can't hurt the player either) unless it throws a bone (requires level mode 0C/0D).
Compatible with the projectile from Dry Bones, Throws Bones in Arc (which this is based of), just make sure you adjust the speeds correctly.

Requested by Anorakun.

name: smwsprites-climber-sprite
title: Climber Sprite
description: My first custom sprite. It follows Mario (depends on extra bit), and climbs up any walls it encounters.

name: smwsprites-climbing-net-door
title: Climbing Net Door
description:
This is a disassembly of sprite 54, the climbing net door.
Includes a define to make it use a dynamic OAM slot instead of the hardcoded one that's used in vanilla.
Everything else is the same.
It's also SA-1 compatible.

name: smwsprites-clock-thwimp
title: Clock Thwimp
description:
Clock Thwimp will go a direction until it hits a wall, and then turn clockwise/counter-clockwise and repeat the process.

Automatically detects walls surrounding it as it spawns in order to immediately start going the intended direction.

name: smwsprites-cloud-ball
title: Cloud Ball
description:
This is a 16x16 horizontally moving sprite, which will try to follow Mario and periodically drop coins and play a sound effect. After dropping a configurable amount of coins, it will disappear in a puff of smoke.

If the extra bit is set, it will successively toss a list of sprites and then disappear. The sound effect for each sprite can be customized.

No GFX included, so you will have to draw them by yourself.

To be assembled with PIXI.

name: smwsprites-cloud-drop
title: Cloud Drop
description:
The ghost-like creature from SMW2:YI. It's similar to the Gusty, but flies back and forth.

Now, the extra bit decides whether the sprite flies horizontally (not set) or vertically (set).

name: smwsprites-cluster-ash-particle-effect
title: Cluster Ash Particle Effect
description:
This is a cluster effect inspired but not directly based of by Ladida's Cluster Effects Pack which resembles ash particles coming from a fire source or lava. The individual particles are spawned using the RNG to make them appear less uniform so good bye, playback consistency!

Read the readme for more information.

Requested by Heitor Porfirio.

name: smwsprites-cluster-bullet-shooter
title: Cluster Bullet Shooter
description:
This is a highly customizable cluster sprite shooter. Please credit me if used, as I spent a lot of time making this as user friendly and easy to customize as possible.

Inspired by Cool or Cruel: Tubular, this was meant to be a publicly available resource for anyone to use so they can make their own bullet hell style level, all with a (hopefully) easy to use sprite.

You can customize things such as the rate of fire, how fast bullets move, whether or not they aim at the player, additional parameters to meet before firing, and more. And this is all possible within a single .asm and .json file, utilizing 9 of the 12 available extra bytes (with plans to utilize all 12 in the future)! I also included a second version of the shooter that only showcases 4 of the extra bytes. While not as customizable, there's less things you have to keep track of and set. This should make it easier to understand how the shooters work at first, then you can expand into the full version.

Check out the readme and .asm file for more information regarding this sprite, as there is a lot to digest. I would recommend reading most (if not all) of the documentation I left, since it should explain mostly everything in great depth.

Along with the gifs below, I designed a Kaizo level a while back showcasing some of their functionality. So if you want a reference video, there's the link. youtube.com/watch?v=uu8VRZxDDtg

Lastly, the only known bugs I'm aware of include SA-1 and carriable host sprites. If you try placing more than 16 shooters on the same screen (I don't know why you would want to in the first place, but I tried anyway), the shooters don't behave with intended behavior. I have no idea why it happens, but it shouldn't be too big of a deal, especially since you can only have 20 bullets on screen at once. As for carriable host sprites, if you feed a baby yoshi to have it grow up, the bullet shooter will latch to big yoshi. If you have it strap onto a regular koopa and jump on it, the shooter will probably latch onto the remaining shell. I may disable carriable attachment in the next update until it's fully fixed.

name: smwsprites-cluster-effects-pack
title: Cluster Effects Pack
description:
Special effects to be inserted as cluster sprites, to spice up any level. Included are falling leaves, rain, fish, and sandstorm. See the readme for more info.

Update 3/29/2020: This now comes with .json files and I added to cluster folder to insert easily.

Update 4/12/2022: Restored old readme and archive structure, made the spawner use extra byte (effectively merging all jsons) and provided an alternative uberASM version.

name: smwsprites-cluster-falling-leaves-effect
title: Cluster Falling Leaves Effect
description:
A cluster effect based of the existing Cluster Effects Pack but with a few gimmicks which ultimately warrants it to be a separate submission.

As implied by the name, this is a visual sprite which replicates leaves falling from trees, bringing in some nice addition for a forest level.

Read the readme from more information.

Requested by Blizzard Buffalo

name: smwsprites-cluster-fire-bowser-statue
title: Cluster Fire Bowser Statue
description:
This is a variant of the Bowser Statue sprite, that can shoot cluster sprites as it's flame projectiles instead of normal sprites. This allows many more projectiles onscreen at once without filling sprite slots, and also has a performance boost compared to the vanilla Bowser Fire sprites (for reference, the screenshots below are demonstrated on LoROM with fastROM disabled).

See the .asm file for customization options and extra byte usage.

Note that while the cluster sprite approximates the vanilla fire sprites as closely as possible, there may be a small difference in player interaction. Additionally, the fire uses ExGFX with 16x16 flame tiles due to limitations with cluster OAM allocation.

name: smwsprites-coin-game-cloud
title: Coin Game Cloud
description:
This is a disassembly of the coin game cloud, sprite 6A.

Now SA-1 hybrid.

name: smwsprites-coin-game-cloud-s-coin
title: Coin Game Cloud's Coin
description: This is a disassembly of extended sprite 0A in SMW, Coin Game Cloud's Coin.

name: smwsprites-coin-muncher
title: Coin + Muncher
description:
It's a coin and muncher recreation in sprite form. You can put it on foreground without overwriting it. It also has some other behavor options.

My first ever sprite submission. Nice.

Credit is optional.

V.1.2.3. Changelog is in readme.

name: smwsprites-coin-shroom
title: Coin Shroom
description:
